Predict the number of recurrent events in a window, by rolling episodes forward

Source: R/predictRecurrentCount.R
predictRecurrentCount.Rd

Experimental. For a patient at the start of (or partway through) an episode of a gap-time recurrent-event model fit with buildRecurrentEpisodes, predicts the distribution of the number of recurrences in (prediction_time, prediction_time + horizon], together with the probability of dying in it, by Monte Carlo: every patient is simulated forward n_sim times, episode after episode, until the window closes or the patient dies. predictRisk() answers "is the next event a recurrence or a terminal event, and when"; this answers "how many recurrences".

Usage

predictRecurrentCount(
  data_predict,
  long_fit_all,
  survival_fit_all,
  prediction_time,
  horizon,
  time_variable,
  survival_variable_all = list(),
  survival_trans_function = list(),
  episode_variable = "episode",
  next_covariates = NULL,
  stay_lengths = 0,
  n_sim = 200,
  max_stages = 10,
  bandcount2 = 100,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

data_predict

The rows of the patients' open episode, as predictRisk() takes them (for example the long_data rows of buildRecurrentEpisodes() for each patient's last episode, whose gap is NA): one data.frame used for every biomarker, or a list of data frames, one per biomarker, as buildRecurrentEpisodes() returns for a list data_long; one patient per id: more than one episode for the same patient is an error. A patient whose gap is not NA and lies below prediction_time counts as no longer at risk, and is an error too rather than a silent zero. The patient's last row (in the first data frame that has the patient) supplies the covariates of later episodes.

long_fit_all, survival_fit_all

Fits from longitudinalSub and survivalSub, on episode data.

prediction_time

The time (on the episode clock, as in predictRisk()) the prediction is made at: 0 at discharge.

horizon

Length of the window after prediction_time, in the same time unit.

time_variable

Name of the time variable of the longitudinal sub-model (e.g. "time_in_episode").

survival_variable_all, survival_trans_function

As in predictRisk.

episode_variable

Name of the episode-counter covariate (default "episode"); used only by the default next_covariates, and ignored if the data has no such column.

next_covariates

Optional function(row, k) returning the one-row covariate data frame of the episode k episodes after the open one (k = 1, 2, ...), given the patient's last row of data_predict as row. The default adds k to episode_variable, but not beyond the largest episode number in the data the survival sub-model was fit on: past it the fitted effect of the counter is an extrapolation (a hazard that grows with each earlier recurrence would be multiplied a hundredfold or more by episode 30), and the simulated paths would run on through ever shorter episodes.

stay_lengths

A numeric vector of non-negative stay lengths (the time between a recurrence and the discharge that restarts the process), resampled with replacement. 0 (default): none.

n_sim

Paths simulated per patient.

max_stages

Most episodes drawn per path (including the first); paths still running at the cap are counted as they stand, with a warning.

bandcount2

Event-time grid size passed to simulateTrajectory.

seed

Optional integer seed; the caller's random number stream is left unchanged.

Value

An object of class "predictRecurrentCount.BJM", a list with

summary

One row per patient: mean_count (expected number of recurrences in the window), p_count_0, p_count_1, p_count_2, p_count_3plus, p_ge1, p_ge2, and p_death (probability of dying in the window, outside hospital: a death during a stay is not part of the model, see buildRecurrentEpisodes).

counts

The raw draws: a patients x n_sim matrix of recurrence counts.

died

A patients x n_sim logical matrix: died in the window.

horizon, prediction_time, n_sim

As supplied.

stages

Most episodes drawn on any path.

capped

TRUE if some path was still running when max_stages stopped it (a warning, giving their share, is also given): its later recurrences are not counted, so the counts are slightly low.

capped_fraction

The share of all simulated paths stopped by max_stages (0 if none).

Details

Each simulated path goes as follows.

  1. The current (open) episode's event time and type are drawn with simulateTrajectory, from their posterior given the patient's biomarker history in that episode – the same distribution predictRisk integrates, so the first step uses the biomarkers exactly as predictRisk() does.

  2. If the event is a terminal event inside the window, the path ends (the patient dies). If it is a recurrence inside the window, the count goes up by one; a stay length is then drawn (from stay_lengths) and the next episode starts at discharge. If the event (or the discharge) falls after the window closes, the path ends.

  3. Each later episode is drawn the same way, but with no biomarker history – the patient has not been observed in it yet – so from the model's prior given the patient's covariates, with the episode counter advanced by next_covariates. Repeat until no path is still running, or max_stages episodes have been drawn.

Limitation. Only the first step uses the patient's biomarkers. Later episodes depend on the patient only through their covariates (and the episode counter), so any patient-level tendency to recur that is not in those covariates – a frailty – is not carried forward, and the predicted spread of the counts (e.g. the chance of two or more recurrences) will be too small when such a tendency is present. Putting the number of previous episodes, or the length of the previous gap, among the survival sub-model's covariates (and updating them in next_covariates) recovers some of it.

The stay length is not part of the backward joint model, so it has to be supplied. The default, 0, means a recurrence takes no time (a tumour recurrence, say); for hospitalizations pass observed stay lengths (they are resampled with replacement).
